findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the no-LLM deterministic fallback's per-criterion decision rule co-located with the verdict contract: state the `met` value assigned to criteria with NO banked verdict (e.g. met:false, mirroring the finalizer prompt's missing-evidence rule) and how the top-level PASS/FAIL is derived from the banked-plus-defaulted set, so it can never emit incomplete coverage nor a false PASS.
evidence: Plan: 'finalize to a full-coverage verdict whenever any progress is banked, with a deterministic no-LLM fallback so a run with banked progress can never die verdict-less'
AC line 1: 'with at least one criterion verdict banked ends in a full-coverage verdict' — a run may bank SOME criteria and leave others never evaluated

src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:420-440 (_validate_coverage): the verdict must return EXACTLY every expected criterion, each with a boolean `met`, or it fails closed — so the no-LLM path must assign a value to never-banked criteria

The LLM finalizer prompt states its rule ('Missing, incomplete... evidence is not enough and must be met:false'; PASS only when every criterion demonstrably met) but the plan gives the no-LLM path NO equivalent rule
ABSENCE: neither the Approach nor the AC states whether never-banked criteria default to met:false (forcing FAIL) or are otherwise handled
findings.finding: AC line 1 references a 'deterministic no-LLM fallback' that 'finalize[s] to a full-coverage verdict whenever any progress is banked', but the plan never specifies the decision rule the no-LLM path uses to assign a per-criterion verdict to criteria that were never banked (the 'unverified remainder' of a partially-progressed run), nor how it derives the top-level PASS/FAIL. The completion coverage contract requires a boolean `met` for EVERY expected criterion, so the fallback must produce one for un-banked criteria; the rule is referenced but not co-located with the verdict schema it must satisfy.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC line 1 ('...with a deterministic no-LLM fallback so a run with banked progress can never die verdict-less'); Approach, 'Banked, batched verification' bullet
scenarios: Primary run banks PASS for 5 of 22 criteria then dies of budget exhaustion; the no-LLM fallback must emit a 22-criterion full-coverage verdict — what does it record for the 17 un-banked criteria, and is the top-level verdict PASS or FAIL?

A banked run where every attempted criterion was met but the run died before reaching the remainder — a naive fallback that copies only banked verdicts would emit incomplete coverage and be rejected by the coverage validator, dying verdict-less anyway
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'Banked, batched verification' bullet, add: the no-LLM fallback emits one record per expected criterion — banked criteria carry their banked met/verdict, and any never-banked criterion defaults to met:false with an 'evidence not gathered' rationale; the top-level verdict is PASS iff every criterion is banked-and-met, else FAIL — matching the existing finalizer prompt's missing-evidence rule and satisfying the exact-coverage contract.
